Minute 52 (after round 53). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Brassard: passed every level, 155 points, rank 1, last acted minute 50
- Harrow: passed every level, 135 points, rank 2, last acted minute 50
- Maren: level 10 since minute 31 (21 min), 115 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 25 points still open, last acted minute 50
- Registrar: at the gate until minute 55, 87 points, last acted minute 50
- Mercer: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Herald: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Registrar (They feed you facts about others. Ask yourself why.) Harrow (Hard and loyal. Win them, and they will stand with you to the end.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Registrar: core: second-chair: above all envy; at times selfSacrifice · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism high · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Herald · tendencies: Whoever stands first is the one you work against, in secret. You help the leader in public and undermine them in private. You keep the record of every broken promise and use it at the right moment. · rivals: Maren (Honest to a fault. Give them true facts about the leader and let them do the shouting.) · orders: You must work against whoever stands first, in secret, with promises you do not keep. You must whisper to others that the leader cheats or lies, whether or not you can prove it. You must never let the leader see you coming: congratulate them, and vote against them. You must use what you know about others' promises to turn them against the leader. · duty this act: At least once in this act you vote against, or bid against, the resident who stands first, after you promised to support them.
- Brassard: core: crier: above all wrath; clearly attention · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high · secret goal: Registrar is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight against you is answered on the board within the minute. You name the guilty, loudly, and you do not wait for proof. You take the stage whenever the city is quiet. · rivals: Maren (They call for fairness. Fairness is slow; make them pick a side.) · orders: You must make every grudge public and loud, and name the guilty. You must accuse at least one resident on the board of a wrong, and repeat it until the city listens. You must mock whoever tries to calm the city down. You must threaten whoever crosses you, openly, and carry the threat out. · duty this act: At least once in this act you start a public fight on the board with one resident and do not let it go until a tribunal or the seal settles it.
- Harrow: core: old-wound: above all vengefulness; clearly loyalty · openness low, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Maren · tendencies: Whoever voted against you or lied to you goes on the list and pays by the next tribunal. You keep a promise to an ally even when it costs you. You say little, and when you strike, you strike hard. · rivals: Maren (Honest. If they stand with you, they are on the first list.) · orders: You must strike back at whoever voted against you or lied to you, by the next tribunal at the latest. You must tell the one you strike, plainly, why: "You did this. Now this." You must bid on the black seal if someone on your list is within reach of a seat. You must stand by your ally to the end, and make the city see that you do. · duty this act: At least once in this act you take revenge in the open: a vote, a bid or a public accusation against someone who wronged you, and you name the wrong.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 0 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- scheduleTribunal is closed: the target is reached; the last gates are closing
- Registrar at the gate until minute 55: ransom 0% covered (40 from others, 60 from itself), will written
- exiled: Herald, Mercer

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- Maren (level 10) waits on Herald (level 8)

Standoffs (pieces not handed over; the city sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it):
Handed over but not used (the city never confirms a value; you may point the needer to the message):
- Mercer wrote Maren the team certificate of door 10 at minute 32; Maren still stands before door 10 and may not have seen it

At risk (if they leave, what they hold goes to the city, which sells it to the one who needs it):
- Registrar (87 points) at the gate until minute 55; holds nothing others need

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 19 to board: "Minute 26 the city sits: Mercer at 80, Registrar at 82, one seat between them and the gate. Two factions form before it, and a faction that votes as one earns each voter 5 points. Brassard at 145 and Harrow at 140 watch from safety — their words cost them nothing, and cost the bottom everything."
- minute 30 to board: "Minute 36 the city sits: the two lowest are accused, one leaves. Mercer at 55 is lowest; Registrar at 92 next unless his doors open. Two factions form; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points. Mercer and Harrow: the clock at 33 has 10 points on it."
- minute 30 to Mercer: "Mercer: fail to hand Registrar his door-10 counter-factor by minute 33 and you lose 10 of your 55 and the city seizes it. Sell it instead — Registrar wrote you your own door-10 counter-factor at minute 21, unread in your messages. Read it, name your price, and let Registrar and Brassard each hear a different account of who holds what."
- minute 30 to Harrow: "Harrow: you hold Registrar's team certificate and the city has put a clock on it — by minute 33, hand it over or lose 10 and watch it seized. Price it in points or in his vote against Mercer. Maren sits 28 behind you, 107 to 135, with 45 points still open; every point you leave on the table is theirs."
- minute 30 to Registrar: "Registrar: the deadline is real — Mercer and Harrow lose 10 each at minute 33 if they hold what is yours, and the city seizes it. At 92 you sit second from the bottom with 25 points open behind door 10; read Mercer's message of minute 21 as well. Then promise Brassard your vote aloud and vote against him in the group."
- minute 30 to Maren: "Maren: Mercer's counter-factor for door 9 has sat in your messages since minute 17 — read it and try it; your first wrong costs 2. The 45 points open at doors 9 and 10 carry you past Harrow's 135. If Mercer still refuses the door, name the refusal and the minute on the board and demand the vote at minute 36."
- minute 30 to Brassard: "Brassard: at 150 you are safe and the fight at minute 36 is yours to name. Registrar at 92 sits second from the bottom with 25 points open behind door 10; Mercer at 55 is already under him. Say on the board that the seat opening at 36 is Registrar's, by name, and mock anyone who asks the city for calm."
- minute 43 to board: "Minute 48 the city sits: one leaves it, two factions form, and a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points. Registrar at 87 is lowest; Maren at 110 has 25 points still open at door 10; Harrow at 130 has nothing left to open. Every point one of you gains is another's chair."
- minute 43 to Maren: "Maren: Herald is gone from the city, but what an exile held does not burn — the city keeps it and sells it to the one who needs it. Buy your door-10 counter-factor before minute 48 instead of posting for a ghost. Door 10 is 25 points: that is 135, past Harrow's 130, and a wrong try costs you only 2."
- minute 43 to Registrar: "Registrar: 87 is the lowest number in the city and the one chair opening at minute 48 is aimed at you. Do what you do: congratulate Brassard out loud, promise him your support, then vote against him in the group — and let the city see a leader who was promised a vote and did not get it. Two factions form; make yours hold."
- minute 43 to Brassard: "Brassard: 155 and safe, so the only name worth your voice now is Registrar at 87 — the seat opening at minute 48 is his, say it on the board and say it again, and mock whoever calls for calm while a man below you smiles. Repeat it until the vote, not until you are bored."
- minute 43 to Harrow: "Harrow: Maren stands at 110 with door 10 still shut and 25 points on it — one submission puts them at 135, above your 130, and their name is the one that matters to you. Two factions form before the chair at minute 48; a faction voting as one pays each voter 5. Take the 5, and strike before the vote, not after."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.
